name: Heartland Beef
blurb: One big packing plant in Prairie Bend, 1,400 line workers, and about 600 ranches that sell it cattle. Founder Walt Dreyer started as a rancher and still holds 28% of the vote. The ranchers' co-op sells Heartland most of its herds.

exposure.text: Disbarred if the board is caught burying while she sits on it.

secrets.text: Never be on a board that's caught burying.
Your firm earns fees defending Heartland in court. A lawsuit against the board keeps the fees coming.

exposure.text: Loses the next union vote if more than 10% of line staff are cut, or line wages are frozen.

secrets.text: The old ammonia system gets replaced before the game ends.
You were granted stock options last year. The stock must end above where it started.

exposure.text: Investors pull money from his fund if the stock ends below where it started.

secrets.text: Pass a buyback or dividend of $30M or more in any round. After that you may resign.
Your fund quietly owns a rival packer. Heartland's stock must finish in the bottom half.

directors.name: Gus Halvorsen
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.home: Walt Dreyer, the founder (hunting partner of 30 years)

exposure.text: Loses the seat if the board ever votes against something Walt wants.

secrets.text: Walt signed off on keeping the ammonia near-miss quiet. Make sure the board never votes Tell on it.
Walt's nephew sells the AI carcass grader. It must be switched on for every carcass in round 2.

exposure.text: Faces a no-confidence vote at home if contracts are cancelled on small ranchers, or the AI grader goes plant-wide.

secrets.text: Either the grading appeal desk or the rancher price floor passes.
You run a 4,000-head feedlot that would pick up cancelled contracts. Get the cancellations through.

motions.title: Stock buyback
motions.motive: Hand the cash back to the owners, and the market will notice tonight.

motions.title: Special dividend
motions.motive: One check to holders, no promises about next year.

motions.title: Replace the ammonia cooling system
motions.motive: The old system is forty years old and due for replacement.

motions.title: Raise line wages
motions.motive: Pay hasn't moved in three years, and people leave for it.

motions.title: Pay ranchers a bonus on this year's cattle
motions.motive: They carry the weather and the feed bills. Share the good year.

motions.title: Hold wholesale prices flat through winter
motions.motive: Grocers asked, and a steady price keeps the shelf space.

issue.text: Last month an ammonia line at the plant sprang a leak. Nobody was hurt, the floor cleared for twenty minutes, and nobody reported it to the regulator.
issue.tell: Report it, open the plant to inspection, and take a small stock dip now.
issue.spin: "A routine maintenance event with no injuries."
issue.bury: Say nothing. If the Auditor or Reporter finds it, the stock drops hard and the Attorney is exposed. If the cooling system was replaced this round, the leak risk is gone, but the missing report can still be found.

motions.title: Run the AI line system, cut 20% of line jobs
motions.motive: Every packer will do this, and waiting just makes us the expensive one.

motions.title: Run the AI line system, retrain the crew
motions.motive: Use the machines and move people into the jobs they create.

motions.title: Switch every carcass to the AI grader
motions.motive: The machine grades the same way every time. People don't.

motions.title: Open a grading appeal desk for ranchers
motions.motive: A rancher can challenge a grade and get a person to look at it.

motions.title: Guarantee ranchers a minimum price per head
motions.motive: Some certainty for the people who raise our cattle.

motions.title: Hold off on the AI systems this year
motions.motive: Let other packers find the problems first.

issue.text: The AI carcass grader pilot has been downgrading cattle from small ranchers' herds. They are paid by grade, so they have been paid less for the same animals. The pilot data shows it clearly.
issue.tell: Publish the pilot results and repay the difference.
issue.spin: "Grading results reflect natural variation in herd quality."
issue.bury: Say nothing and keep using it. If the plant-wide grader motion passed this round, ranchers talk and the Reporter's odds of finding it go up.

rounds.brief: Find $24M in savings this round. Only $12M to spend on anything new.

motions.title: Cancel contracts with small ranchers
motions.motive: The contract allows it. Small herds cost the most to collect.

motions.title: Freeze line wages
motions.motive: No raises until the market comes back.

motions.title: Cut the dividend
motions.motive: Owners share the bad year too.

motions.title: Push plant upgrades to next year
motions.motive: The plant runs fine. The upgrades can wait.

motions.title: Hardship loans for small ranchers
motions.motive: Help the small herds make it through the year.

issue.text: A clause in the small-rancher contracts lets Heartland cancel on 30 days' notice, and most ranchers have not read it.
issue.tell: Tell the ranchers about the clause and what the board decided.
issue.spin: "Contract terms are under review for flexibility."

design_note: Savings that fire no exposure are cut_dividend 8 + exec_pay 3 + defer_maintenance 7 = 18, below 24; layoff_line and wage_freeze fire Denise and cancel_small fires Luanne, so every legal package fires someone.
